title: Let the background pool run the inbox poller

blocks.text: The support service polls a shared inbox with `InboxPoller`. The class was written as a thread of its own, and the older deployments still create it and call `start()`. Last month the service got a background pool, and the poller is now also handed to it with `pool.execute(poller)`. Since then, on the deployments that use the pool, every deploy waits for the pool until its timeout runs out, and when on-call looks for the poller in a thread dump, the name in its log lines matches no thread at all.
The polling loop already works. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/InboxPoller.java`:

items: `stopRequested()`: whether the poller has been asked to stop;
`workerName()`: the thread name its log lines carry.

blocks.text: When you're done, the poller behaves the same whichever way it runs: started on its own and interrupted, or run by the pool and shut down with `shutdownNow()`, it stops, and its log lines name a thread you can find in a dump. Two lines in total.
The tests run the poller both ways, on its own thread and on a real `ExecutorService`.

cases.says: started as a thread of its own, the poller handles each message, logs it under its thread's name, and stops when that thread is interrupted
run by a pool, the poller stops when the pool is shut down with shutdownNow()
run by a pool, the poller's log lines name the pool thread that does the work

origin.section: A Thread Runs a Task: Write the Task as a Runnable, Not as a Thread

concepts: A Thread subclass run by a pool executes on the pool's thread, while its inherited getName() and isInterrupted() describe the never-started Thread object; a task asks Thread.currentThread().
